before:
Ghana's main airport and, for a long time, its only international one. It handled a record 3.62 million passengers in 2025, up from 1.2 million in the pandemic year of 2020, and it has been named Best Airport in Africa in its size band three years running by Airports Council International.

Terminals are simple to explain. Terminal 3 takes regional, international and long haul flights and can handle aircraft as large as an A380. Terminal 2 is domestic only. Terminal 1 is closed and is to be redeveloped as a private aviation terminal.

It is a hub for Africa World Airlines and a base for Passion Air, so onward regional connections are good. Freight is substantial too, with Cargolux, DHL, Emirates SkyCargo, Ethiopian, Qatar and Turkish all flying cargo in.

Worth knowing for a business client: Airport City Accra has grown up around the terminals, with the Marina Mall, the Accra Marriott, ibis Styles and a Holiday Inn all on the doorstep.

The airport was formerly called Kotoka International, a name still in wide use.
after:
Ghana's main airport, which handled a record 3.62 million passengers in 2025.

International flights use Terminal 3 and domestic flights Terminal 2. Terminal 2 is being refitted to take some international flights as well, so check which terminal a client's flight uses.

It is the base for Africa World Airlines, which flies within Ghana and across West Africa, and PassionAir also flies domestic routes from here. For business clients, Airport City Accra has grown up around the airport, with offices and the Marina Mall.

Its name changed from Kotoka International back to Accra International Airport on 23 February 2026, the name it had until 1969. The code is still ACC, and older material may still say Kotoka.

claims.claim: a record 3.62 million passengers in 2025
claims.inAfter: which handled a record 3.62 million passengers in 2025
claims.note: JUDGEMENT CALL, flagged for the owner. The regulator publishes the parts, not the total: 2,539,034 international passengers plus 181,826 transit (its international table) plus 903,227 domestic passengers to and from Accra (its domestic table) makes 3,624,087, exactly Wikipedia's infobox figure. The same sums give about 3.40 million for 2024 and lower totals for every year back to 2010, so 2025 is the highest in the regulator's series. The international table is national, though Accra carries almost all of it.
